study: Culliney et al. 2019 (Integrating English / LiLAC genre-pedagogy CPD; EEF trial)
eval_evidence: Independent EEF evaluation by Sheffield Institute of Education, Sheffield Hallam University; the evaluators are explicitly distinct from the Enfield LA delivery team ('the evaluators would like to thank... the Integrating English delivery team').
developer_evidence: The program developer (Enfield LA School Improvement Team) developed AND delivered the CPD: 'The programme was developed and delivered by Enfield LA School Improvement Team'; 'the Integrating English course was delivered by qualified teacher trainers recruited by the Enfield programme team.'
cascade_evidence: Enfield's trainers delivered the CPD to the participating Year 5/6 teachers directly at five regional hubs (teachers then taught their own pupils); no train-the-trainer / lead-teacher re-delivery hop reported.
counterfactual_evidence: Two-armed cluster RCT with a business-as-usual control (control schools continued normal English provision); design note and exec summary describe BAU comparison.
coaching_evidence: Delivery = centre-based CPD workshops at five regional 'hubs' with a virtual learning environment between sessions; teachers produced schemes of work. No in-class coaching component reported.
student_dose_evidence: Intervention is genre-pedagogy CPD that changes the teacher's English instruction (schemes of work delivered by the teacher in normal lessons); no tutoring, pull-out, or extra student dose.
maturity_evidence: Single cohort taught Integrating English across Year 5 (2016/17) and Year 6 (2017/18); the KS2 (Writing/Reading/GPS) outcomes were measured at end of Year 6, i.e. after a prior Year-5 implementation year. (Teachers were new to it in Year 5.)
